commentary: Both kings have castled and remain behind their kingside pawns while the central pawn structure remains intact. White's queen knight and queen bishop remain on their original squares so queenside development is incomplete even though the king has castled. Black has brought both knights toward the center and developed the kingside bishop while the queenside bishop remains undeveloped. The active bishops occupy central diagonals with lines toward the opposing kingside pawn shields although those pawns remain protected. The queen pawns support the king pawns and help hold the central structure in place before any central pawn exchanges. The queens remain on their original squares rather than taking advanced posts and their scope depends on the intervening pieces. The rooks remain behind the pawn formations with limited access to open files so a suitable file opening would change their activity. Development and pawn support are both relevant when comparing White's available continuations and forcing replies still need concrete checking.
